newsitem.title: CHILE: Brazil sees Cemig sale price over $1.2bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees Cemig sale price over $1.2bln.

text.p: The government of Minas Gerais expects to receive over $1.2 billion from the sale of one third of state power company Cemig, with interested bidders, including Chilean and U.S. firms, said a senior state official.

"We are looking for at least book value...33 percent of voting stock is worth at least $1.2 billion," deputy governor Walfrido dos Mares told Reuters before a meeting with Chilean Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
The sale will be through an auction in the Sao Paulo stock market in December, he said.
Dos Mares said the government has not struck a private deal with investors and all interested companies will have compete in the auction.
Cemig's common shares rose more than 10 percent in Sao Paulo on Thursday on talk the government had reached a deal with a Chilean firm, said analysts.
Companies which have expressed interest include Chilean distributor Chilectra, its sister company generator Endesa, Southern Electric and a group of Brazilian companies, said dos Mares.
Minas Gerais officials held a meeting with Chilectra executives at the Brazilian embassy in Santiago on Thursday to explain the terms of the sale, he said.
"We want a specific strategic partner not great number of shareholders," said dos Mares.
"Chilectra may be this if they succeed in the auction in the stock market in December."
With 5,000 megawatt capacity and five million customers, Cemig is currently owned 84 percent by the state. The state's share will fall to 51 percent after the sale, said officials.
